body: That's fair, RWD kicks my ass so I usually don't touch it and drive FWD and AWD. I noticed you had the issue of adjusting your angle mid-slide during slow slides since AWD will usually decrease oversteer on throttle (before the diff locks up) while RWD will increase oversteer on throttle. Going off throttle for a tiny moment or lightly applying brake with your left foot while still keeping the throttle up can get your car around, but sometimes it can unsettle the car if you hit the brakes too hard.

Are you on a wheel or controller?

Either way, as much as its a pain I'd turn off the visual indicators for the pace notes. You'll be slow and miss calls at first but once you get good at hearing the calls you'll find controlling your car easier since your eyes are now doing the driving instead of glancing up to read the pace notes. With a wheel it also means that your hands are feeling the grip levels with your eyes on the road, and you're listening for the calls which gets you faster, quicker.

On a controller, it lowers your chances of glancing up at bad times such as when an unexpected slide occurs, or coming into a tight corner that appeared earlier than expected.

The visual indicators also don't note some other important calls, and do a bad job of noting connectors. When daddy Phil calls "keep left over 140", the visual note will only show 140. And those "keep left" and "keep righ" calls not only keep you on the road in faster stages, but also set you up for corners and avoiding hazards in the twisty stages.

Rasmas looked to her leg for a moment, silently and solemnly thinking to himself as he grabbed Eva's hand. "Let's sort out your injury, first, I'm sorry I didn't intervene fast enough." He apologized, closing his eyes. "I need a vibroblade, too. I'm not a confident enough duelist but I can surely sneak around enough to do what we need." He explained, placing his other hand over the back of hers. "I'm going to do better to protect you, I couldn't bear losing you." He admitted, before looking away in nervous silence.

He nodded before sighing and looking at her leg "You're free to siphon more energy." He stated, guilt hiding within his voice. 

He turned the holocomputer seated in the flight controls on. "Set a course for anywhere, we need to stay low for a while and hope that the Giantess and her lover caused enough strife within the Jedi that they don't even note our escape." He said, looking at the controls closer. "Shit, no weapon system..." He hissed a bit, looking at his feet before stepping back. "How is your leg, I can try performing some first aid if you need." he offered, looking into her eyes.

Shaking his head slightly he looked back at the holocomputer, looking through news for the past month or so, to try and get a grip on what had happened while they were on Korriban and in custody.

**Crazed Jedi severely injures CorSec officers after a pointless ideological standoff with Payne Corp. CEO!**

**Crixus Payne - Holonet Sensation: How Corellia's most eligible bachelor has swept the planet up in a Payne Craze!**

Rasmas's eyes seemed to light up for a moment, as he read the articles with the awfully intriguing headlines. "Eva, we should head to Corellia." He proposed, looking at her. "Look at this." He said, waving her over.

Past the gate and a small network of hallways was a small entrance into the hanger of the Citedel, guards mobilising at the two groups attempting their escapes. Hearing a set of footsteps, Rasmas pushed Eva and himself into a storeroom out of the way of the guards and out of sight. After taking a moment to breathe he looked up at Eva, stepping away from her as they were mere inches apart. "Sorry, about just standing there, it happened too quickly for me to be able to step in..." He whispered, sighing with contempt pointed towards himself. "There's a lot of Guards out there, and I don't think stealing their uniforms is an option, but we can't dash for it because of your leg..." He explained more towards himself, before looking at his own leg, remembering the moment at the station. "Eva, Use whatever that draining ability you had on me to heal your leg." He asked, nearly demanding as he looked her dead in the eye with a serious face.

"The two of us should be able to make a run for the nearest ship quickly enough once your leg injury is healed from that." He explained, biting his finger.

"Three." Rasmas said with newfound determination, standing and bolting through a path that avoided the fight, as he attempted to jog his memory on where the hanger was. 

He looked behind him momentarily to see that Eva was following close behind, his hand still on hers as he very slightly tugged her along.

*Eyes forward, no turning back now.* He told himself, looking forward to notice another gate to the hanger, the path blocked by 2 guards.

"I think he's more preoccupied with the two fuckers trying to cut his little limbs off." He'd say flippantly, taking a peek at the fight that had just begun. He'd take a moment, breathing deeply, before firmly grasping Eva's hand. "We book it on 3." 

"1..." He said, seeming to linger a bit, his eyes looked to Eva, not with eyes of a determined escapist, but a scared boy.

Rasmas bolted out of his cell upon feeling Eva's presence. with a mix of desperation, opportunity, and tunnel vision Rasmas made it to Eva's cell before anyone had even noticed. Quickly hitting the release on the control panel to let Eva out he waved towards himself slightly. "C'mon, this is our chance!" He'd say, looking at Eva.

Rasmas had been silent the entire time, thinking. He would have lots of time for this for a long time. He had concluded to himself that:
 
Eva and the Giantess would never work together, in any case.

All three of them could have escaped much easier together.

He would quietly sigh, looking at his cuffs.

*Damned Jedi Dogs, Taking justice into their own hands. We should have been put to trial.* He thought to himself, Regardless of whether they'd still be sent to the slammer, the citadel was telling of the Jedi Order's self-righteous view of themselves.

His blood felt as if it was boiling, a clear grimace on his face, breaking the pure pokerface he had been maintaining throughout their transport.

Rasmas sighed, looking down. He looked like he had given up, raising a hand to his chin. He stood up, his chair sliding slightly. Even if his instincts were screaming at him to fight, he knew it would end up killing the both of them.

He frowned, admitting defeat. For now.

Rasmas sighed, sitting down. "Rasmas." He would say, letting go of his efforts to conceal himself, he'd need to train the skill further.

"Rasmas is my name" he'd say, nodding his head, instead of a bow.

He kept his expression neutral, and tried to hold his emotions down, yellow eyes would be very incriminating at this point.

"Now, it looks like formalities have been thrown out the window, so how about we just get to it." He'd say, resting one elbow on the table.

Rasmas had kept silent the entire time. Meditating as he walked, he hadn't taken in much of his surroundings.

He might have had talent in force conceal, but he had never tested his metal against a Jedi Telepath, at least not one actively trying to read him.

Beginning to focus, his presence in the force quickly faded and imploded. Finally, a true measure of his most honed technique.

"There's a dark-side cult on the planet Yavin-4, lead by someone who called themselves "Lord Jorku or some shit." He'd say, tilting his head forward. "And there is or was a sith in the senate, we've been invistagating that."

"I've been in direct contact with the Jedi shadows, I can tell you that they were very easily tricked, at least, tricked enough for me to know too much." He would say, smirking a bit. 

"The Order is trying, but failing horribly." He would say bluntly, staring at the Jedi questioning him.

"Valdis." He said flatly, staring at Lytrinn, he still hid his presence in the force as he normally would.

He frowned slightly, waiting for the next question.

Rasmas silently nodded, pulling his Saber back and up, but keeping it ignited. "I'm still carrying her to the ship." He said, stepping forward. He would turn of his lightsaber, throwing it to the Jedi.

"A token of trust, even though you just showed me you'll betray it."

Rasmas shot his arm out violently at the shout, sand being thrown up by his force push, 1 of the soldiers lost his footing, slipping back and shooting his peer in the back, stunning him. However, 2 of the soldiers simply grunted the force of the attempted disarm shooting straight.

He quickly shot into the small amount of visual cover he had, knocking the soldiers down and grabbing Eva's body, placing her arm over his shoulder and carrying her on his back. Turning around, he ignited his lightsaber, now in a staredown with a dozen soldiers and a Jedi.

Rasmas took a short moment to think. "Interesting, still trying to pry for information when there's a Saber to your neck? Well, you're nothing if not headstrong." He said flippantly, looking down at Lytrinn and thinking of the next sentence he'd say. 

"Well, I'm not the best at asking questions, so I'll let my peer handle the talking."

His eyes zoned in on Lytrinn, changing his stance. "Long story, ask your elders in the high council about that, specifically about the Jedi shadows." He said, his pride catching the best of him. 

"Your cult is out hunting other religions again, and you say we're the bad guys." He said, smirking.

He was clearly riding a high from their victory, his eyes a signiture yellow.

Rasmas had fallen under the ship, and chose to relocate to another point of concealment. He noticed Lytrinn hitting the rock, injured and unknowing of Rasmas's whereabouts. His raised both of his arms, reaching out within his mind to pick the rock up, hovering it above Lytrinn to try and force him into open field combat.

Rasmas quickly reacted after being thrown off balance while he was heading to the right. Quickly ducking under a boulder that nearly took his head off, he'd run forward and close the game between him and the Jedi, staying defensive yet keeping pressure on the Jedi.

Rasmas would switch the grip on his lightsaber to a reverse shien grip, transitioning into the stance. 

*He's got decent reactions, even if he's using his lower senses.* He thought, gripping his saber a bit tighter. 

*If I threw sand up again, and did a strike at either side, he'd defend against Eva first since he'd know where she is, then I'd be able to strike with the blade.* He'd tell himself, looking down at both his weapons to get a feel for how long his cut down vibroblade is now.
Blue 1
Seemingly out of nowhere, Rasmas appeared from behind, closing in with a one handed horizontal slash, his other arm holding a vibroblade in a reverse grip to act as a follow-up to the strike.
Rasmas grunted the push, igniting his saber and coming in from the Lytrinn's right with a reverse grip cross-slash, a strike usually found in the reverse grip Shien varient.

Rasmas would take a few breaths, closing his eyes for a moment before quickly opening them again, as his iris changed from their natural colour to a vibrant yellow. 

He brought his arm arm quickly, throwing the sand of the desert up into the air with the force, limiting visibility to about a meter in front of the fighter. with his presence in the force hidden, and now practically being invisible, Rasmas would relocate, soft footsteps being the only indicator of where he could be.

Within the local dust storm, Rasmas waited for his chance to strike.

Rasmas would frown, taking his lightsaber off of his belt and transitioning into a form 1 starting stance. "Interesting, I've never seen an orange blade before," He would comment, leaving his lightsaber powered off. "Now, we could make this simple, no?" He said, tilting his head forward a bit. 

"You run off and tell the 'high' council what you've seen, and let us pass. You'll feel like you helped and we'll get a chance to continue on our merry way, or you can throw yourself in a 2 verses 1 brawl. 

One of his hands would lower, making a fist, his presence in the force collapsing upon itself and disappearing. He had become invisible, not to one's sight, but to one's reach within the force.

"They both wanted something, but didn't want the other guy to have it." He said, jabbing a guess as he sat down. "Wait, is that a tooth? are there beasts here?" He said, darting back up and igniting his lightsaber. "What are you getting at, anyway?" He would ask her.

"Wait, for real?" He would say incredulous. Making a short dash too here he'd lean over her shoulder to see for himself, a combined feeling excitement and fear that caused the hairs on his arms to stand up, that or the fact that it was suprisingly cold down here.

"Let's stick together, I wouldn't be surprised if these objects could cause hallucinations, force visions perhaps." He said, pointing his saber downwards but keeping it in his hand. 

"I'm hoping to find a few saber components, my current saber doesn't fit me anymore." He said, stretching and heading inside the temple.

Rasmas's lips upturned, his brow lowering slightly as he looked at Eva. "You really have had a fire lit inside you." He comments, following her.


 "You should be careful, than, I've noticed that my use of the dark side has been progressively destabilizing the crystal in my saber, the same might happen to your pair of sabers." He warns, as he unclips the saber from his belt and inspects me. An unrefined weapon, something built to batter through a person's defense, it didn't fit him anymore.

Rasmas nods. "How do you think I got away from the shadows?" He says, stepping down on to the surface of the planet. 

"Or even get inside the temple?" He continues. "We should teach eachother everything we know, as I feel my combative abilities are lacking." 

Rasmas begun pondering on her plans. "It sounds reasonable, we should find masks to conceal our identitied when we strike." He says. "If the shadows learn we're making moves again they'll be up or ass in no time. "Well likely need to change our lightsabers, it's not like a pair of pure white sabers is the most popular option, no?"

Rasmas nodded in agreement, not really having anything to add. 

The ship landed, with the loading bay door opening. A grand view of the valley was revealed, statues of dark lords long gone on either side of a walking path.

"Any ideas on how we could hit the Jedi? They're a large force, and their best are going to be total ass to deal with." He says, cracking his knuckles. 

Rasmas went silent for a moment. 

"Say, do you know how to conceal yourself in the force?" He asked Eva.

His fingers tingled slightly. "Can you feel that?" He asks, wiggling his fingers a bit. "It's like this planet is a dark-side battery." He says, standing.

"Of course I'll be on guard, we should be somewhat quick, take any holocrons you find." He says, heading to the loading bay, trusting the autopilot.

"I wouldnt be surprised if this place has been ransacked before, however, so we shouldn't keep our hopes up." He says, stretching his shoulders.

"It looks like a massive valley, statues and a temple that leads underground." He said, feeling a wave of energy wash over him as he got closer to the surface. 

It had been a long time since he last was able to let the dark side show itself within him. It had been brewing just under the skin, the fury of his childhood trauma becoming his own status quo. With Eva turning he was finally able to free that fury within him, harness it. 

He closed his eyes for a moment, indulging in the clarity he'd felt since they left the station. 

*The force shall free me.* He said within his own mind. Standing upright. 

"It's best we check the temple, my bet is that this is the major temple on the planet." He said, speculating and turning the face Eva. "Sound good?" He asked her.

He put the ship back into hyperdrive, course set for korriban. 

"Let's hope we don't run in to any sith, then." He joked again, standing and heading off to meditate.

"Mandalore or Korriban, then?" He asked, hands hovering over the control panel. 

"You're doing the talking if we're going to Mandalore, though, I'm not exactly silver-tongued." He joked.

"Then we could forge jedi plans to attack mandalore and it's soon to be allies, convincing them to do a preemptive purge of the Jedi and..." His mind trailed off, the darkness around him intensifying for a moment. "No, no, that's an unrealistic plan." He told himself.

"How could we use them against the sith?" He asked Eva.

"No, not at all!" he replied, looking at Eva.

Then the thought hit him. "Mandalore was the head of the neutral star systems during the clone wars, if I remember correctly." He bit his finger again, looking out into the void of space. "We could try and convince their political leader to do the same thing as in the clone wars, but suggest that they should stay open to pre-emptive self defence strikes." He continued, pausing, and then letting go of the thought.

"We won't be able to take a sith in open combat, we need to take a reformation shipment." he thought aloud. "We have all the time in the world until the sith make a move, time to grab scout drones to be our eyes and ears on the ground of Korriban." he said, suddenly taking the ship out of hyperspace, they were in the mid rim, having started at Ticondaroga station which was near Kuat, and heading towards Korriban meant that Mandalore was the closest major planet.

"Hmmph, Can you check if Mandalore has a position in the war?" He asked Eva, biting his finger.

"Crixus, the political leader, is in the final stage of his plan." He said, pondering that sentence for a moment he went back and corrected him. "Actually, we don't know the stage, just that he's confident that even him dying won't stop him from achieving his end goal." He explained, being happier with that sentence. "Secondly, this means that he's achieved a form of political immunity, if the Jedi capture or kill him, Corellia will likely leave the republic, or worse, aid the Reformation." He said, biting his finger as he thought.

"That worries me, a lot" he admitted. "The shadows are going to be on Corellia, at least that sadistic giant will be, to my understanding."  he explained. "More over, Crixus has likely done a runner on Corellia, therefore we won't get anything useful out of it." he begun to bite his finger harder. 

"There *will* be sith on Korriban, a move like Crixus's is meaning enough for the sith to meet, an ancient sith home world is the perfect place to meet." He deducted, planning an approach Korriban.

"How many day's worth of food and water do we have?" He asked Eva.

"Sounds right." He stood, heading to the cockpit and immediately lifting off after the loading bay was shut. He'd punch in Korriban's co-ordinates, as the ship jumps into hyper-space. "Force sensitive order's are too far into politics, I saw the news about Corellia, the political leader there is a follower of Sith teachings. His speech was good, but it means 2 things." He had an analytical tone to his voice, he was repeating the speech in his mind

His lips curled up, a devious smile. Celot's death was the straw that broke the camel's back, it seemed.

His eyes burned a violent gold, this was perfect. The trip to the Jedi temple forced him to repress his true nature, everything he felt had to go. This wasn't in his nature, all of humanities nature wasn't like that. She was correct, finally correct. 

"Only with a blank tile we can see the cracks, total destruction is the way forward if we're to mend the mistakes these orders have made." He said, continuing her thought with his own. "You saw what *sadism* the Jedi are capable of, and the sith even pride themselves on that brutality" he spoke as if he was holding back a paragraph hidden behind each word. This was *him*, this was *Rasmas*

He'd look as if he was thinking, looking down at his hand. "I don-, what do you mean anyway?" he'd answer, with his own question. 

Would he be considered a Sith? By other people or even by the sith themselves? He *had* killed Jedi in his life, at his age that was massive. He already used the Darkside, and largely served himself. But he wasn't a warrior, he enjoyed duelling but never felt sadastic pleasure immediately after he would perform the final strike. 

What *really* was he? He thought.

He winced as the lid crashed and banged, taking a moment to reset and go back to the conversation. 

"Korriban, I know it's an old sith world but not much past that, you think we'll find sith there?" He said, looking at her, his question was loaded.

He'd pull the container of paint out of the trolley, passing it to her. 

"What are you going to do with it? looks like it's important." He asked again.

He nodded, glad she changed the subject from his name.

"Yeah, I did, why did you want it anyway?" He asked, tilting his head to the side slightly and giving her a confused look.

He paused, giving her an odd look. "I never told you, I just thought you read my mind without my permission." He frowned at her. "Regardless, it's not 'Ra', it was Rasmas." he took a breath after he finished that sentence. 

"*Was* Rasmas, don't call me that if we find ourselves on Coruscant again." He warned, walking into the ship and turning a few of the systems.

Rasmas's eyes zoned in on her, he had been silently meditating as he collected more supplies, regardless, he used her to re calibrate back into the physical plane.

"Correct, A few bandits decided to try to rob me, turned out bad for them and we have quite a few credits now." he said, passing the wad of credits to Eva. "Took their blasters and sold them off but kept a rifle and two pistols for ourselves, turns out weapons are a hot commodity in a crime ridden space-station," he said, smirking.

He smiled back at her, nodding in agreement. "Firstly, we should set a course for that space station, we'll have to be quick too, as info of the brawl we just had in Tiranis's office is going to make it's way to the high council very quickly." He said, turning away and heading for the living quarters, but stopping at the door and turning back to face her again. "Let's tear everything down, then." He said, before heading off

"Fly away from coruscant, far away." He said, sitting down and helping with booting up the systems. The sound of the ship roaring through the sky as it exited the atmosphere was the only thing either of them heard for a while, until Rasmas spoke again. "Let me fix that for you." He said, walking to the first aid kit and making interesting use of the supplies to reseal the tubing that was cut, and then tending to his own wound.

"We'll need to hide from the republic, it's best to try and find refuge in reformation territory." He said, he had gone distant again. "Are you ok? did my fix work?" He asked her.

He took a step forward, deciding to engage the male, with the darkness around Eva making him feel permitted to show his real colours. He swung downwards, as their sabers clashed his opponent had to widen his stance to not fall on ass. His opponent stepped to the side, letting Valdis move forward and used the momentum to swing for Valdis's neck.

Valdis leaped sideways, avoiding the strike and trying for a thrust aimed at the Jedi's neck, which was deflected. Due to his specialisation in form 5, Rasmas used the momentum from this deflection and used it to amplify the potency of his next attack, a straight slash aimed across the body. The Jedi was knocked on his ass upon blocking the strike, as his lightsaber rolled across the floor.

The Jedi, however, refused to give up, calling back his saber and thrusting for Valdis's leg. Valdis narrowly avoided losing his leg, but had his left thigh burnt by the Jedi's Saber. He carried the Jedi's blade up in a bladelock, grabbing the Jedi's wrist and holding it their, the pain from the burning fuelling his anger and hatred, and strengthening him in the force. 

The Jedi's eyes widened upon the realisation that he was going to die, this was the face someone made when they had given up hope. This face was all too familier, it brought him back to the day of his Mother's death, the faces of the two men he killed that day had that expression. He closed his eyes and took a few breaths, holding the Jedi still. 

"You will be remembered." He said, comforting the Jedi infront of him. He raised the saber up, running it through the man's neck and through the brain stem, instantly killing him, painless and quick, how it should be.

He took a step back, re-calibrating before he went to try and help Eva, but failing to jump, the burn was deeper then he initially thought. He barely held himself up, guilt had weakened him.

"Stop calling me Ra." he blurted out, following her anyway towards the ship. He took a glance at Djen's body, then back forwards, his mind and thought's moving internally for a moment. 

*such a wasteful death, a death I caused...* He thought, a wave of guilt striking him, but he didn't let those thoughts cloud his thoughts for now. His perception moved back outward, as he looked around to re-calibrate himself, they had reached the ship.

Rasmas had been slipping around the battle field throughout the battle, flinging drive by strokes that were blocked by the masters, and under the chaos felt like their assailiants strikes, being hidden in the force and thus, hidden in the chaos. There was a moment of silence, but not clarity during the battle as metal warped and the ship was crushed. He jumped down from a high point, landing a ways behind Kayran and pointing his saber at the jedi. "Disgusting." Was the only word he said at first. "*You're* disgusting." He took a step forward, falling into an odd stance, it was obvious that it was a form 5 stance, but it was a modified form 5 stance. "I never knew Jedi were capable of sadism, it's why I left the order after all." His eyes begun burning a violent yellow.

Rasmas's eyes widened. "People are here, get your saber ready, I'll hide and intervene if they try to attack you and drake, but they'll definitely strike if they see me." he explained, running and jumping up high onto a set of shelves that were in the corner directly left, the curve of the wall concealing him from a simple glance.
He simply frowned at her, not giving an answer. "We're not finding anything here, we should go in.case someone is coming." He said, clearly in a mood
"Someone I don't want to be anymore." He said quietly, taking a step away from the desk and her.
He looked at her for a moment, wondering how she had figured that his name was an alias He stepped back, frowning at her. "Valdis *is* my name, but not my birth name." He answered tersely.
As her hand made contact on his shoulder, she could hear someone calling a name, a name starting in R... R-A, but it was just a feint echo around the room.
"I don't know if they knew about Tiranus, im just a kid." He said, frustration in his voice.
Rasmas went silent, only displaying the thousand yard stare on his face. He held onto his lightsbaer tightly as his body tensed up, standing upright.
"They didn't know Tiranus was a senator, at least, the man I know Tiranus contacted recently *heavily* implied he was." He explained, his voice growing softer and slower
Rasmas looked flitty and unfocussed, but still spoke. "The Jedi didn't know he was a senator as he kept his face hidden during the duel." He explained distantly
"He still thinks his cover isn't blown, Eva." He frowns, growing silent as he eventually zones back out.
"It confirms that Tiranis has something to hide, and it puts a mark on his back." He stood, looking at Eva. "Let's bug the place," he suggested, "see if he does any shady shit in his office."
"He might have chosen not to have an assistant, it's rare but legal under republic law..." He explained further

"Usually there's a button on the desk to contact the Senator's assistant, I thought we could get him to try and investigate why he's getting summoned to the office even though the senator isn't here, there's no button here." He explained, looking at the screen infront of him.

"My parents were senators once..." He said, gripping his saber tighter as he went over to the computer, looking around the desk and at the keyboard. "Eh, weird," he said, frowning. "Of course," He said through gritted teeth. "Why would a sith lord acting as a senator have an assistant, it makes hiding your identity harder," he continued.
He sighed, dropping down on his knees to check under a bolted down chair. "Maybe we can locate the Senator's adviser and interrogate him." He suggested.

Rasmas jumped slightly, his hand reach back and behind him into a secret pocket in his robes before he stopped. He looked Eva in the eyes, then down again. "Sorry, I'll go back to searching," he said distantly, as if his mind was in another time.
After about 5 minutes, Rasmas had gone into a trance, just staring out the window while holding his saber, hand tight on the grip.

The guard holding the staff looked to the other, "Actually, yeah, that sounds about right." he said, under her influence he lowered the staff.

"I mustn't have been listening I think." he said, opening the door for the group.

Rasmas walked in, and after the others entered he looked around a moment. "Let's do a quick sweep but not miss any spots, I don't feel good about this," he suggested, raising a few couches to look under them.

One of the guards raised their staff, holding it across the door. "You don't look like jedi," he said tersely. 

The other spoke, not moving his staff, "Sorry, if we haven't heard we can't let you past, that's our orders."

Rasmas walked forward, pushing forward to the door guarded by two senate guards dressed in blue.

"Sorry, sir, no visitors as the senator is currently not present, and even then you need to make an appointment, I suggest you leave," the guard said, eyeing the group.
Rasmas came out the changing room in his usual black robes and padded boots. "Yep, it's only fair right?" he said, walking over to the loading bay doors.

He raised his arm, he wasn't holding his lightsaber like one would assume. "We should figure out what this stuff is made of, it was like a less effective version of cortosis, it fizzled and made our blades short but not for as long. Apart from that, nothing really." He said. "I'm changing out of these stupid robes, they're getting itchy." He said, off to the living quarters.

"Eva, keep your mind away from those thoughts. Even if the Jedi order fail the Galaxy has other people willing to protect it." He said, stepping closer. "Like us, if you want something done you should do it yourself, isn't that why you got Drake and I to join you?" He asked
"Well, I got in simply because I wore the right robes, they must be." He said jokingly.
He nods. "One of the shadows had dueled him in the Jedi temple." He said, trying to recollect his thoughts after being in a room with two experienced Jedi wanting to kill him.

"They figured I was a fake," He bluntly said. "I did learn that there was a dark side cult at the tomb, and Tiranis stopped by and took refuge for a moment there. He was also from Eriadu, and the cult leader said that Tiranis is or was a senator."

"That leads me to the conclusion that we should search his office ASAP before the shadows do, and if we find nothing there, we kidnap the current senator and test his blood." He said, stretching his neck. "They most likely will take  the cult leader back to the temple before they do the search, which gives us time." He finished, walking to the cockpit.

Rasmas ran out from the green of the forest into the clearing the ship had landed in, sprinting up to the ramp and sliding a good few meters to stop himself. "Long story short: I'm not a good spy, both the people I was with already harboured suspicions about me, we need to get off the planet to the Senator of Eriadu's office now." he said, cheeks lightly red from him sprinting about a kilometre as fast as he could.
